search_results.title: How a sundial tells time
search_results.snippet: A sundial tells the time from the shadow cast by a pointer called the gnomon. As the sun moves across the sky the shadow sweeps across hour lines.

search_results.title: Aligning the gnomon
search_results.snippet: For accurate readings the gnomon must point at the celestial pole, so its angle equals the local latitude.

search_results.title: Sundial time vs clock time
search_results.snippet: Sundials show apparent solar time, which can differ from clock time by up to about 16 minutes over the year. The correction is called the equation of time.
